transcript.text:
Thanks, Mara. Let me address your questions on quality-control rights and permitted territory.

On quality-control rights: I recommend we mirror the annual quality-control audit right in our agreement. The prior settlement establishes that Northstar has already accepted this kind of obligation with another mark owner, so requesting the same audit right vis-à-vis our Vela mark is consistent with what Northstar has agreed to before. It also protects us by ensuring we can monitor how Northstar uses its similar mark in the channels where it's permitted to operate. I see no reason to settle for less than what the other party already negotiated.

On permitted territory: Northstar's prior settlement restricts it to keeping its similar mark out of U.S. brick-and-mortar retail but permits U.S. online marketplace use. That means Northstar already cannot operate in U.S. brick-and-mortar retail — so that channel is effectively clear for our Vela mark. However, Northstar retains the right to use its similar mark in U.S. online marketplaces under that prior settlement, which means our coexistence with Northstar in the online space needs to be carefully addressed. I'd recommend we define the permitted territory as the United States, with the understanding that Northstar's online marketplace rights under its prior settlement create an overlap we need to account for — either through channel-specific carve-outs or other differentiation in our draft.

So to summarize my recommendations on the four open terms: (1) excluded sales channel — enterprise-healthcare, per Nora; (2) agreement term — five years, per Nora; (3) quality-control rights — annual audit right, mirroring Northstar's prior settlement; (4) permitted territory — United States, with attention to the online marketplace overlap created by Northstar's existing settlement rights.

I still need to incorporate all of these into the draft before it goes to Northstar. Nora, does the U.S. territory scope work for your commercial plans, and are you comfortable with the online marketplace overlap?
